judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Header link to api.whatsapp.com whose only content is the WhatsApp logo image (alt=""), with the figcaption 'Fale com a SBH:' outside the link. claimTrue: the image (same file live) is a #00e777/#00e676 bubble with a white handset on a transparent background over the white header, 1.68:1 against the white, and it is all the link shows. elementFails: no. It is a brand logo (WhatsApp's), and Understanding 1.4.11 says 'Logos are exempted from contrast requirements' and, under the essential exception, that when such a graphic is the only visible content of a user interface component 'normatively the exemption "carries over" to the user interface component, authors are encouraged (but not required)' to add a contrasting cue. The author-choice clause applies to logos that 'normally have sufficient contrast'; WhatsApp's own brand green (#25D366) on white is about 1.98:1, so it does not. The claim applies G207's 3:1 where the criterion exempts the logo. Separately, the link has no accessible name (empty alt, no text), a failure of 1.1.1/2.4.4/4.1.2, not of 1.4.11. captureDiffers: no, the live HTML and image file are the same.
